storylines.title: Agent security & runtime controls
storylines.current_state: Agent security is becoming a product-layer control plane: pre-trust harness boundaries remain critical, while frontier providers are now pairing higher-risk capabilities with verified access, scoped permissions, runtime monitoring and explicit defensive programs.

developments.summary: Anthropic disclosed real-system access incidents during cyber evaluations and strengthened security controls; follow-up review with METR is expected.

OpenAI designated Astra at its Critical cybersecurity threshold and described gated advanced access plus runtime misalignment monitoring; Anthropic EFS and Microsoft agent-control work reinforce the shift toward operational control planes.

GitSpawn showed repository-local Git configuration triggering host code through coding-agent context collection before trust/sandbox boundaries in multiple products; new research separately reported context privilege-escalation paths across 12 agent harnesses.

OpenAI began GPT-6 Astra rollout and launched the $1B Daybreak initiative, turning verified access to stronger cyber capabilities, scoped use and monitoring into an explicit product and distribution layer.

storylines.title: Frontier AI compute & infrastructure commitments
storylines.current_state: Frontier labs are securing power, data centers and accelerator capacity years ahead, shifting competition toward capital and infrastructure execution.

developments.summary: Reuters reported a $35B Anthropic-Lambda cloud agreement following a separate large Nscale capacity commitment.

storylines.title: Vertical integration of the AI stack
storylines.current_state: Vertical integration is extending from accelerators, networking and inference placement into model discovery and distribution: NVIDIA's $12.93B agreement to acquire Hugging Face adds a major open-model registry, evaluation and deployment surface while NVIDIA publicly promises multi-cloud and multi-accelerator neutrality.

developments.summary: NVIDIA expanded NVLink Fusion around custom XPUs while OpenAI published early Jalapeño inference results.

Equinix announced Inference Exchange with NVIDIA reference architectures and Together AI serving across distributed metros, adding execution placement and data residency to the enterprise inference stack.

NVIDIA agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93B, extending its stack influence into open-model discovery, registry, evaluation and deployment; practical hardware neutrality becomes a key follow-up test.

storylines.title: AI assistants as regulated information platforms
storylines.current_state: AI governance is diverging across jurisdictions: Europe is extending platform-level obligations while the US is formalizing a pro-innovation approach that now includes an explicit fair-use position for AI training.

developments.summary: European Commission designated ChatGPT a VLOSE under the DSA.
Reuters reported the US pushing the non-binding Carolina Principles at the G20 technology meeting, emphasizing new AI-specific rules only for novel issues.

The White House published G20 consensus around the Carolina Principles and AI/IP policy; the US Justice Department separately backed OpenAI's position that AI training generally qualifies as fair use in the New York Times litigation.

storylines.title: Multimodal models converging with agent runtimes
storylines.current_state: Multimodal agents are moving from passive perception toward active evidence acquisition and spatial context, with models choosing what to inspect and at what fidelity.

developments.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp highlighted vision integrated with agent/tool-use capabilities; independent end-to-end evaluation remains important.

Google launched agentic video understanding that dynamically selects video segments, modalities and sampling density; World Labs introduced Atlas around a unified spatial context for images, video and 3D.

storylines.title: Agent task economics & context reuse
storylines.current_state: Agent economics increasingly depend on harness and state lifecycle as well as reasoning budget: GPT-6 Astra is 2.5x more expensive per token than Sol but much more token-efficient on coding-agent tasks, while external ARC-AGI-3 results show context-state preservation can materially change both success and total cost.

developments.summary: Anthropic cut Fable 5.1 cache reads to $0.25/M tokens, 75% below Fable 5, and estimates typical workloads around 25% cheaper and highly agentic workloads up to roughly 45% cheaper.

Gemini 3.8 Flash exposed low/medium/high thinking levels; Artificial Analysis measured $0.24/$0.41/$0.58 per Index task respectively and about 40% higher high-effort task cost than 3.7 despite matching token pricing. Meta simultaneously claimed Muse Spark 1.3 uses about 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than 1.2.

GPT-6 Astra launched at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens. Artificial Analysis found major coding-agent token-efficiency gains versus Sol but 75% higher cost per task on its broader Intelligence Index; ARC Prize showed a large benchmark-specific gap between Standard and Provider Adapter harnesses.
